title: Support both FIELD_VALUES and RESOURCE_TABLE when changing a search ResultFormat
answers: Why does user search still need to handle RESOURCE_TABLE after switching to FIELD_VALUES?
How to add a new ResourceSearchRequest ResultFormat without breaking older servers
ParseResults fails with 'unsupported search result format'
body:
Symptom: switching a search request to a new ResultFormat (e.g. FIELD_VALUES) breaks responses from older/unupgraded unified-storage servers that still return RESOURCE_TABLE.
Root cause: the request's ResultFormat is a client preference, not a guarantee; the server may still answer with the older format, so the response must be parsed according to its own result.GetResultFormat(), not the format that was requested.
Fix pattern: in the response parser, switch on result.GetResultFormat() (UNSPECIFIED/RESOURCE_TABLE vs FIELD_VALUES vs any new format) and dispatch to a dedicated parse function per format; keep the table-parsing path alive as the compatibility fallback.
Constraints: applies whenever a ResourceSearchRequest.ResultFormat is changed or a new format is introduced; do not remove the RESOURCE_TABLE parsing branch just because a newer format is now requested by default.
applies: pkg/registry/apis/iam/user/search.go ParseResults and any other handler that sets ResourceSearchRequest.ResultFormat
